mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns during inflation spikes are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not exceed 0.3% in at least 40% of months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS labor compensation growth of at least 0.5% signals wage strength, which elevates expected corporate profits and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth rate ≥ 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with PAYEMS growth ≥ 0.5% for 2 months, 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of instances (rolling IC < -0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing index (≥ 2.0% month-over-month decline) indicates weakening near-term supply capacity, which amplifies demand-driven equity premium and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During INDPRO contractions ≥ 2.0%, 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) or IC > 0.10 over a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both HOUST retail sales and RSAFS financial sector demand (each ≥ 1.5% month-over-month) creates a dual-demand signal that elevates risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both proxies meet the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (IC ≤ 0.05) or the joint IC is flat (< 0.02) across multiple such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.50% for three consecutive months indicates a prolonged easing cycle, which amplifies discount rate compression and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During such FEDFUNDS easing, 60-day forward returns are not outperforming a 5% risk-free rate benchmark (IC ≤ 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE unemployment (≤ 3.5% from the prior month) suggests labor market tightening, which raises expected wage growth and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During UNRATE declines ≤ 3.5%, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (IC ≤ 0.05) or the effect is only observed during high-inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GDPC1 consumer demand index (≥ 4.0% month-over-month) in the context of a falling INDPRO signals an imbalance between demand and supply, which amplifies equity risk premium and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When the trigger occurs, 5-day forward returns are not negative (IC ≥ 0.10) or the interaction IC is flat (< 0.02) across multiple such events.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a 'normalizing' FEDFUNDS path where the 6-month average FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.2 percentage points from the prior cycle peak, combined with a steady CPIAUCSL below 2.0%, predicts a neutral monetary stance and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 6-month average FEDFUNDS up ≥ 0.2pp from prior cycle peak AND 6-month average CPIAUCSL < 2.0%
failure_condition: During such normalized regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (IC > 0.05) or the effect is only present during high-inflation episodes.
